title: Rook SE quick journal and action list
content:
Context: working on Juniper Health pilot (PHI scoped). Compact running notes for the week, config snippets, and action items. Quick reference for handoff to Maya if I get pulled into infra incident.

Morning recap (2025-10-14):
- 09:15 sync with Juniper SRE (Tom). Confirmed VPC peering timing: they want the peering created 10/20 PST.
- 10:00 internal with infra: kernel upgrade window might conflict with Juniper's prod cutover; propose canary lane instead.
- 11:30 demo prep for 10/15: reduce token budget for demo model to cut cost.

Top-level todo (priority ordering):
1) Network & security
   - Finalize VPC peering checklist. Items left: route table tag convention, shared-services firewall rule ID. (ACTION: me)
   - Confirm KMS entry format for Juniper: they use AWS KMS (alias juniper-prod-key). Need key policy snippet. (ACTION: Liam)
2) Model selection & quantization
   - Run quick perf matrix between bert-qa-4b-int8 and gpt-style-3b-fp16 on 128-token sequences. (ACTION: run perf job using se-perf runner, ETA 10/16)
   - If 4b-int8 latency < 40ms p50 and quality delta < 3% on sample set, propose bool flag to use quantized model for demo.
3) Observability & alerts
   - Add route-level SLO for Juniper: p95 < 200ms for staff tier. Add tracing header propagation in proxy. (ACTION: Maya)
4) Rollout plan
   - Canary config: 5% traffic -> canary model variant, automated fallback to baseline on error rate > 1%. Draft canary policy in console (see snippet below). (ACTION: me)

Unresolved questions:
- Juniper compliance: do they need logs sent to their Splunk instance, or is S3 export enough? Waiting on legal confirmation (JIRA SE-4321).
- Are they ok with our default tokenization? They have some legacy pre-tokenized payloads; may need a preprocessor hook.

Quick config snippets (copyable):
- Canary rollout policy (console JSON):
  {
    "strategy": "canary",
    "canary_percent": 5,
    "monitor": {
      "error_rate_threshold": "0.01",
      "latency_p95_threshold_ms": 250
    }
  }

- Minimal KMS policy snippet to hand to Juniper for cross-account decrypt (they will paste into console):
  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [{
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Juniper-Redwood-Role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }]
  }

Notes from demo prep:
- Trim system prompt, use 80-token context in the demo to keep costs predictable.
- Add sample user prompt set: 6 queries that exercise PHI redaction flow. Saved as se/juniper/demo-prompts-2025-10-15.txt (attached to Confluence page).

Meeting follow-ups (action owners):
- [Jordan] Draft VPC peering ops checklist + route table tags by 10/16.
- [Maya] Add tracing header PR + test in staging by 10/17. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/1124
- [Liam] KMS policy confirmation + add to onboarding doc by 10/18.
- [Jordan/Maya] Draft canary policy + unit test for failover by 10/20.

Logs / commands I ran today (for reference):
- se-perf run --model bert-qa-4b-int8 --seq 128 --concurrency 8 --target juniper-testnet > /tmp/bert-int8-128-20251014.log
- aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/juniper-prod-key --query Policy > /tmp/juniper-kms-policy.json

Quick risks (for CSM):
- Risk: Juniper expects request-level PII redaction in their upstream service; we need to ensure our logging scrubs correctly before S3 export. Mitigation: add log-scrubbing lambda in pipeline and include sample redaction tests.

Scratch notes to self (short):
- If perf numbers look bad, try sequence bucketing before batch bundling.
- Keep demo to 3 scenarios only. Nothing noisy.
- Add small section in handoff doc: "What to do if VPC peering fails" (simple rollback steps).

Reference links: Confluence page (team-run): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SE-ROOK-JUNIPER
Jira: SE-4321 (compliance question), SE-4367 (canary infra ticket)
Slack threads: #se-rook, #juniper-health-ops

Status note: still draft — will tidy this before handing to Maya on 10/17.

End of quick journal entry.
